replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to reduce the dimensionality of a dataset while preserving as much variance as possible. First, standardize the data. Then, compute the covariance matrix. Next, calculate the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix. Sort the eigenvalues in descending order and choose the top k eigenvalues. The corresponding eigenvectors form the principal components. Project the original data onto the new feature space formed by the principal components. As for the mathematics, it involves linear algebra and calculus, but you don't need to be an expert to understand the basics. There are many user-friendly tools and software that can perform PCA for you.
